author: reek
body: The two halves bisect deliberately. If sha512 is wrong the hash lines fail and everything downstream is explained by them. If the hash lines pass and pubkey fails, the defect is in the curve arithmetic and not in the digest.

author: reek
body: The published signature must verify, and a signature with one byte disturbed must not. A verifier that always answers True looks exactly like one that works, so the tampered line is what gives the passing line its meaning.

author: reek
body: TEST 1 signs an EMPTY message, which is its own edge and worth keeping for that alone. Our signer must reproduce the published signature byte for byte, and the verifier must accept it.

author: reek
body: A caution, earned twice while writing this file. Two different hand-written versions of this signature were wrong -- one with a nibble inserted at byte 39 that shifted the whole tail, one with a tail belonging to another vector entirely -- and each time the verifier rejected the bad signature and the rejection was briefly read as a defect in the verifier. Converting hex by machine does not help when the hex itself is misremembered.

author: reek
body: What settles it is that verification IS the oracle here: a signature that verifies under a given public key and message is, barring a forgery, the genuine one, and a signature off by a single nibble does not verify. So the pair of lines below is self-checking in the way that matters, and the outside anchors elsewhere in this file -- the FIPS digests, the base-point encoding, TEST 2's published signature -- are what keep the whole from being agreement with ourselves.
